html:
Willemstad, the capital of Curacao, grew around Fort Amsterdam, built by the Dutch after they took the island in 1634. It lies on both sides of the narrow channel into the Schottegat harbour.

Its rows of brightly painted gabled houses along the Handelskade recall Amsterdam in Caribbean colours. The floating Queen Emma Bridge, opened in 1888, swings aside to let ships pass.

For centuries the town was a hub of trade, smuggling and the slave trade, home to Dutch, Sephardic Jewish, African and Latin American families, whose mixed speech became Papiamento. In 1997 its historic area became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The great oil refinery beside it shaped its 20th century.
